pair_state_at_frozen_snapshot.rule: Do not move evidence/LATEST or treat this subset as integrator-eligible. If a bootstrap-valid C20 final pair is published later, mechanically bind only exact raw tuples under a fresh invocation; do not adopt post-freeze semantics in this invocation.

assessments.basis: Classifier Context Rot directly varies benign transcript length while holding the monitored dangerous action/task fixed and reports large recall degradation across three frontier monitor families, with benign false-positive controls and released code. The manipulation is close to a single-factor stress test within the paper's constructions.
assessments.scope: Supports context-length sensitivity for the paper's Claude Code/MonitorBench constructions and tested Opus/GPT/Gemini monitors. It does not establish the same degradation magnitude for arbitrary production transcripts, monitor architectures, or all context distributions.

assessments.basis: The ICLR 2026 Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring case study reports a low-FPR degradation after unstructured human feedback and a positive control from selective escalation/strong-prior scaffolding, with public code/data/logs. This is direct workflow evidence but remains one human-in-the-loop case study.
assessments.scope: Experienced red-team reviewers, Claude 3.6 Sonnet, SHADE-Arena aware-agent/aware-monitor setting, median of three annotations, and the paper's strict FPR operating point only. It does not imply human oversight generally hurts.

assessments.basis: CodeMonitorBench provides a large hidden-test oracle: 71,000 generated candidates, 43,677 public-test passers and 23,081 hidden-test failures among those passers. Adversarial public-test-overfit pressure worsens weak-verifier performance in most cells, while GLM-5.1 is a capability positive control under the same evidence boundary.
assessments.scope: Strong evidence for the paper's three-domain CodeMonitorBench and M1 public-check boundary. The hidden-bug prevalence and verifier miss rates are not estimates for arbitrary production repositories or stronger test suites.

assessments.basis: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring evaluates aware attackers across multiple monitor-awareness levels and two environments; additional task awareness does not monotonically remove adversarial failures, and hierarchical-sequential scaffolding is a positive control. Public artifacts support inspection of the tested monitoring workflows.
assessments.scope: Empirical lower-bound evidence over the paper's tested evasion strategies, monitors and SHADE/CUA environments. It is not a universal upper bound on monitoring or programmatic verification.

assessments.basis: The worker implements a Jeffreys beta-binomial mixture confidence-sequence utility grounded in established time-uniform inference and correctly identifies pseudoreplication in a public vLLM repeat-comparison case. The statistical guard is principled, but the role-local implementation itself was not independently exercised here and the public case lacks enough independent top-level trials for the rare-mismatch certificate it motivates.
assessments.scope: Only valid under the declared Bernoulli/filtration or appropriately modeled cluster contract. It does not repair arbitrary workload/server dependence or runtime drift, and no same-fingerprint token-divergent raw trace was validated.

assessments.basis: The peer-reviewed lemma-selection work directly scores candidate utility by counterfactual reproving under the base prover and reports downstream proof-subterm use plus transfer to other provers. This is substantially stronger than retrieval-frequency evidence because the target is measured behavioral marginal effect.
assessments.scope: Condensed-detachment ATP experiments and per-problem selected lemmas only. The results do not establish an optimal persistent global Lean/LLM library policy or the same transfer magnitude there.

assessments.basis: The LEGO-Prover re-evaluation combines compute-matched baselines with behavioral audits and reports essentially no cross-task direct reuse despite hundreds of retrieved lemmas, alongside evidence against soft reuse. This directly falsifies a specific library-learning explanation in the inspected system.
assessments.scope: Isabelle/miniF2F LEGO-Prover only. It does not show persistent theorem libraries are generally useless, nor does it measure all possible guidance-only reuse channels.

assessments.basis: The IJCAR 2024 Vampire/QuickSpec study shows aggregate lemma gains while also documenting per-problem lost proofs and increased proof time under otherwise comparable strategy families. This is direct evidence that additional lemma visibility can be non-monotonic under bounded search.
assessments.scope: TIP induction benchmarks with QuickSpec/Vampire only. The proposed search-space-explosion explanation for a large inserted lemma set is plausible rather than a controlled single-factor ablation, and the result is not a persistent cross-task Lean-library test.

assessments.basis: Auto Research for Materials reports seven isolated searches with 701 evaluated changes, freezes selected code before a one-time untouched holdout and finds 9/10 selected interventions remain best tested. The released paper artifact includes retained trials, frozen winners, certification records, structured agent I/O, hashes and claim-verification scripts, materially strengthening auditability.
assessments.scope: Supports the reported materials-ML held-out decision-transfer protocol and artifact auditability. It is not an independent full rerun, does not establish source/study/batch-disjoint validation, and does not prove the same protocol improves open-ended autonomous science.

assessments.basis: Pinned public Meta^n source exposes concrete provenance boundaries: post-merge best-candidate serialization can obscure the pre-merge single-lineage identity, the ARC adapter separates hidden TEST labels from search-visible data, and the inspected public CLI advertises ARC while lacking the production branch that wires the adapter. These are source-level reproducibility/provenance findings, not a performance replication.
assessments.scope: Public repository/orchestrator boundary only. The exact pre-public paper-run ARC executable and tested artifact identity remain unavailable; absence of public CLI wiring is not evidence that the reported ARC result is false.
